note: Triennial election of the Cookstown rural district councillors, 1939. Nominations were received on Tuesday 18 April 1939 by Mr. James M'Cammon, clerk, as deputy returning officer. 'There will be no contests for any of the seats on the new Cookstown Rural Council ... All the candidates are returned unopposed' (Mid-Ulster Mail, 22 April 1939, p. 9). Sixteen divisions are recorded. No nomination was received for Beaghmore, 'at present represented by Mr. James Loughran. In all probability he will again take his seat'; as its retiring member he was deemed re-elected. No party labels are printed. No poll was held; the folder date is the provisional Tyrone polling day. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Munterevelin' to Munterevlin (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Cookstown Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Munterevlin; the rounds were filed as Munterevlin (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967); Munterevelin (1939). This round was filed as 'Munterevelin', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (munterevelin) answers with a redirect to this one.
